exercises.prompt: Envy of someone’s blessings is really a complaint against whom?
exercises.explanation: Before envy becomes a feeling about a person, it is a hidden objection to Allah’s distribution.

source.text: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?

options.text: Society in general
The envier’s family
The blessed person
Allah - the One who distributed His bounty

exercises.prompt: What is ghibta, and how does it differ from hasad?
exercises.explanation: Ghibta is clean aspiration - the Prophet’s hadith allows this kind of "envy" in two cases only.

source.text: There is no (harmful) envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah gave wealth and he spends it in truth, and a man whom Allah gave knowledge and he teaches it.

options.text: Watching others succeed without caring at all
Another word for hasad
Wishing for a similar blessing without wanting it removed from the other person
Copying someone’s exact lifestyle

exercises.prompt: Which two situations did the Prophet describe as the only acceptable form of "envy"?
exercises.explanation: The only permitted envy is the desire to do MORE good - not to have more things.

source.text: There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and he spends it in the right way, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom and he judges by it and teaches it.

options.text: Aspiration for athletes and actors
Aspiration for whoever has more followers
Aspiration for someone who spends wealth in truth and someone who teaches knowledge
Aspiration for famous people and rich people

exercises.prompt: What is hasad (envy)?
exercises.explanation: Hasad targets the blessing itself: the envier wants it gone, not matched - that is what the Quran seeks refuge from.

source.text: And from the evil of an envier when he envies.

options.text: Feeling sad when someone is harmed
Wanting a similar blessing for yourself
Resenting someone’s blessing and wishing it were removed from them
Being competitive at work

exercises.prompt: Why did Iblis refuse to prostrate to Adam?
exercises.explanation: The first act of hasad in history was the first act of defiance - envy and arrogance travel together.

source.text: He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay.

options.text: He did not hear the command
He was busy in worship
Arrogance and envy of Adam’s honored station
He thought Adam had wronged him

exercises.prompt: Who does envy damage first?
exercises.explanation: The envier’s chest is the first casualty: anxiety, insomnia and bitterness arrive long before the "revenge".

source.text: And from the evil of an envier when he envies - the envier’s harm starts with his own state.

options.text: The person who carries it - it eats their peace before it reaches anyone else
Nobody - it is just a feeling
The envier’s friends
The envied person only

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet warn envy does to good deeds?
exercises.explanation: A warning worth taking seriously - with an honest note on its grading, since scholars differ about this narration.

source.grading: da’if (weak per some scholars; some grade it hasan)
source.text: Envy consumes good deeds the way fire consumes wood.

options.text: It consumes them the way fire consumes wood
It makes them count double
It has no effect on deeds
It delays them until Ramadan

exercises.prompt: An envious person watches someone else’s blessing fade and feels relief. What did the Prophet guard against with daily dua?
exercises.explanation: Envy wishes loss on others; the cure is asking Allah to protect your own blessing rather than delighting in anyone losing theirs.

source.text: The dua of a Muslim for his brother in his absence is answered; the angel says: Ameen, and may you have the same.

options.text: That we never hear bad news
That we gain more followers
That our enemies fail
That our good be not lost or transferred

exercises.prompt: Your cousin buys the house you also hoped for. What is the clean alternative to hasad?
exercises.explanation: The two permitted kinds of "envy" turn the sting of comparison into fuel: aspire to give and to teach.

source.text: There is no envy except: a man given wealth who spends it in truth, and a man given knowledge who teaches it.

options.text: Ghibta - be glad for them and ask Allah from His bounty for yourself too
Find something wrong with their house
Compare their loan terms critically
Never visit their home again

exercises.prompt: You catch yourself comparing followers and feeling resentment. What breaks the habit?
exercises.explanation: The Quran promises: gratitude grows blessings, and resentment only consumes the blessing of the envier.

source.text: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor].

options.text: Trading comparison for gratitude - and making dua for the people you envy
Working until you out-perform everyone visible
Deleting the app and staying offline forever
Avoiding anyone more successful than you

exercises.prompt: What did the Prophet say to say when you admire something in someone else?
exercises.explanation: Asking for barakah is the opposite of hasad: you are praying the blessing stays and grows.

source.text: When one of you sees something pleasing in himself, his brother or his property, let him ask Allah to bless it.

options.text: Compliment only if they deserve it
Point out its price
Say nothing - truth brings envy
Make dua for barakah in it

exercises.prompt: A classmate posts a great exam result and your chest tightens. What does iman ask of you?
exercises.explanation: The Prophet’s measure of love: wanting for your brother what you want for yourself - even in exam results.

source.text: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

options.text: Keep the anger and let it grow
Wish for them what you love for yourself - and ask Allah for your own share
Mute them immediately - problem solved
Comment something backhanded

exercises.prompt: You make dua for someone in their absence. What did the Prophet say happens?
exercises.explanation: This is the exact medicine for hasad: you cannot fear someone’s blessing and sincerely pray for it at the same time.

source.text: Whoever makes dua for his brother in his absence, the angel says: Ameen, and may you have the same.

options.text: You gain only half
The dua is ignored
The angel says: Ameen - and you get the same
The person must be told

exercises.prompt: You feel envy toward your sibling’s success. What is the specific, active Sunnah move?
exercises.explanation: Repel the bad impulse with a good one: dua for the envied person rewires the heart from resentment to generosity.

source.text: Repel evil with that which is better; then the one who had enmity between you and him may become like a close friend.

options.text: Share their news negatively with others
Compete silently and say nothing
Deliberately make dua for them to have even more
Ignore the feeling until it fades

exercises.prompt: Followers, salaries and house sizes keep changing. What scale did the Prophet point to?
exercises.explanation: Allah does not look at your forms or appearances; He looks at your hearts and your actions - the only scoreboard that holds still.

source.text: Allah does not look at your bodies or your appearances, but He looks at your hearts and your actions.

options.text: Notability in society
The size of one’s friend group
Hearts and deeds - not appearances or numbers
Bank balances and property

exercises.prompt: Where does the cure for envy start?
exercises.explanation: Once you settle that the scales belong to Allah, the enemy of the envier becomes a paper tiger.

source.text: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? And We had already given... which is better than whatever they accumulate.

options.text: Collecting more than the other person
Avoiding all social contact
Explaining your own goodness to people
Knowing the blessing is Allah’s distribution - and being content with your share

exercises.prompt: Your younger sibling breaks something of yours and you feel anger boiling inside. What should you say?
exercises.explanation: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil. (A’udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim). Said when anger flares - anger comes from the devil, and refuge is sought with Allah.

source.text: I know a word which, if he said it, his anger would go away: "I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil."

options.text: I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed devil.
May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah; there is no strength or power except with Allah.
In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
